sources.note: Lialina essay loads; describes the mid-90s web as bright, personal, slow and under construction.
Vernacular Web 2 loads; lists Under Construction signs, outer-space backgrounds, MIDI, blinking New! buttons, glitter, repeating backgrounds, no clear structure.
Cameron's World loads; GeoCities 1994-2009, over 38 million pages, spaces always under construction.

fixes.problem: Neocities' own site and about page are not in this style and the about page never mentions GeoCities; it is a host, not an example of the look.
fixes.correct: Keep Neocities as a host only if labelled that way, or link a specific hand-made Neocities page that shows the style.

note: Claims check out; only the Neocities example is loose.

sources.note: system.css page: System OS 1984-1991, based on System 6 as the final monochrome version, 59 x 20 px rounded-rectangle buttons.
Hyperallergic loads and supports Kare's black-and-white pixel icons; it says nothing about dither patterns, which S3 covers.
Stylesheet loads: striped title-bar gradient, 2px border plus 2px offset shadow on .standard-dialog, checkerboard pattern, Chicago/Geneva/Monaco font faces.

fixes.problem: 'System 6 was the last monochrome version' repeats the library's shorthand. System 6 already ran in colour on the Mac II (1987) and let icons be coloured; only its window frames stayed black and white.
fixes.correct: System 6 was the last version whose standard window chrome was black and white; System 7 (1991) colourised the interface on colour Macs.

fixes.problem: The code sets font-family to Chicago and Geneva, Apple's proprietary system typefaces, as the thing to use.
fixes.correct: Use an open-licence bitmap or pixel font and describe Chicago/Geneva only as historical reference.

note: Accurate look; soften the 'last monochrome' line and drop Apple fonts from the code.

sources.note: Toastytech: bevelled 3d look popularised by NeXTStep and OS/2 2.0; explains the single Start button.
98.css page plus its stylesheet: silver background, the exact inset-shadow bevel, raised borders turn sunken when pressed, navy-to-#1084d0 title bar, 75 x 23 px buttons, pixel MS Sans Serif.
Kent Sullivan's paper (mirrored): Start menu as a single-button home base, taskbar for switching windows.

note: All claims verified; 98.css values live in its stylesheet rather than the page text.

sources.note: Mac OS 8 HIG: system-wide platinum appearance checkbox people can switch on or off.
Mac OS 8 HIG: platinum is the default; Appearance control panel offers accent and highlight colours; default font Charcoal, Chicago for layout.
Mac OS 8 HIG controls chapter lists push, radio, checkbox and bevel buttons.
Wikipedia Appearance Manager: built for Copland, keeps System 7 shapes and positions, shades of grey, Charcoal default with Chicago option, palettes for progress bars, scroll thumbs and selections.

fixes.problem: 'replacing the mostly black and white System 7 look' overstates it: System 7 already shipped a colourised interface on colour Macs.
fixes.correct: Platinum made a grey, 3D-shaded look the system-wide default, replacing System 7's mostly flat chrome (lightly tinted on colour Macs).

note: Well sourced; one comparison with System 7 is overstated.

sources.note: Apple press release, 5 January 2000, Macworld Expo San Francisco: luminous, semi-transparent buttons, scroll bars and windows, fluid animation.
Wikipedia Aqua: blue/white/grey palette, gel effect, pulsing blue default button, pinstripes then white, drop shadows instead of frames, Lucida Grande, Genie effect, red/yellow/green window buttons.

note: All claims verified against both sources.

sources.note: XP.css 0.2.6 stylesheet: blue title-bar gradient, 8px/7px top radii, Trebuchet MS title, #ece9d8 body, 3px button radius with #003c74 border and white-to-beige gradient.
Wikipedia: Frog Design contracted for the visual identity, saturated colours and rounded corners, blue/olive green/silver, Trebuchet MS titles and Tahoma, Fisher-Price nickname.

fixes.problem: Code sets font-family 'Trebuchet MS', a Microsoft-owned typeface, and copies Luna's exact title-bar gradient.
fixes.correct: Keep the gradient as a recipe but name an open humanist sans (with Trebuchet only as a system fallback).

note: Facts verified; code leans on a Microsoft typeface.

sources.note: Nicol 2006: green the unofficial colour plus saturated blues, oranges, pinks; rounded corners and rounded logo type; FREE in a starburst; big text; white space.
TNW 2008: unwritten set of guidelines with gradients, round corners, mirror effects, a badge and 48px+ key text.
Frutiger Aero Archive 2025: Web 2.0 Gloss most common from about 2007 to the early 2010s; gradient button with a hard stop at 55% and a reflection added via ::before; reflections under objects.

fixes.problem: 'starburst badges shouting Free or Beta': neither S1 nor S2 ties starbursts to Beta; S1 only names Free.
fixes.correct: Starburst badges shouting Free (Beta labels were common too, but cite a source or mark [inferred]).

note: Strong sourcing; one unsupported word.

sources.note: Wikipedia: Encarta 95 and MSN 2.0, Media Center, Zune, introduced as Metro with Windows Phone 7 in 2010; Swiss design, transit signage, light/thin font, lowercase headings, live tiles, motion acknowledging taps.
principles.design: authentically digital, bold vibrant colours, typography, content before chrome. It does not mention shadows, bevels or 3D.
NN/g 2012: completely flat, no pseudo-3D or shadows, low density, overly live tiles backfire.

fixes.problem: 'No faux textures, shadows, bevels or 3D icons' is cited only to S2, which does not say it.
fixes.correct: Cite S3 (NN/g: no pseudo-3D or lighting model to cast shadows) alongside S2.

fixes.problem: Code uses 'Segoe UI' (Microsoft's proprietary typeface) and #0078d7 (Windows' default accent blue).
fixes.correct: Use an open humanist sans in light weight and a neutral saturated tile colour; mention Segoe only as history.

note: History verified; fix one citation and remove Microsoft font and accent colour from code.

sources.note: Android docs: Dynamic Color added in Android 12, source colour, five key colours, 13-tone palettes, light and dark schemes.
Compose docs: Material You and M3 Expressive; M3 Expressive complements Android 16; shape scale square to fully circular.
Google blog: springy animations, neighbouring notifications respond to drag, blurred shade, shape-morphing on Wear OS.
Compose graphics-shapes: rounded polygons and Morph between shapes.
Google Design: 46 studies, 18,000+ participants; colour, shape, size, motion, containment; key elements spotted up to four times faster.

fixes.problem: '46 studies with 18,000+ people found key elements spotted up to 4x faster' merges two findings: the 46 studies are the whole research programme, the 4x result comes from one eye-tracking lab study.
fixes.correct: Research ran 46 studies with 18,000+ participants; in one eye-tracking study people spotted key elements up to 4x faster.

note: All sources support; one research statistic is conflated.

sources.note: Acrylic doc: recipe of background, blur, exclusion blend, colour/tint, noise; seams edge to edge; no accent text on acrylic.
Mica doc: opaque, samples wallpaper once, neutral when inactive, base layer plus content layer.
Geometry doc: 8px top-level containers, flyouts, dialogs; 4px in-page controls.
Engadget 2017: Fluent unveiled at Build; five elements light, depth, motion, material, scale.
Wikipedia: codename Project Neon, revamp of Metro, Reveal highlight discontinued with WinUI 2.6.

fixes.problem: 'the noise and tint set it apart from plain glassmorphism' is not in S1; it is the author's comparison.

note: Thoroughly sourced; tag one comparison as inferred.

sources.note: Apple newsroom, June 9 2025: translucent material that reflects and refracts, specular highlights, tab bars shrink on scroll, concentric controls, iOS/iPadOS/macOS Tahoe/watchOS/tvOS 26.

WWDC25 session 219 transcript: lensing bends and concentrates light where older materials scattered it, highlights layer with moving lights, thicker material when larger, concentric nesting in window corners.
HIG Materials: don't use in the content layer, use sparingly, regular and clear variants, 35% dark dimming layer for bright content.
NN/g, 10 October 2025: legibility and contrast problems, motion for motion's sake.

note: Every claim verified against Apple's own pages.

sources.note: HIG Designing for visionOS: windows, volumes, immersion, passthrough, eyes and hands.
HIG Materials: no distinct Dark Mode, glass adapts to luminance behind it, vibrancy; change log shows visionOS guidance added June 21, 2023.
HIG Windows: default window is an upright plane of unmodifiable glass with specular reflections and shadows; ornaments; opaque backgrounds feel heavy.
HIG Eyes: hover effect on gaze; 16 pt margin or 60 pt between centres; avoid repeating patterns filling the view.

fixes.problem: 'glass windows ... that light up when looked at': the hover highlight is on interactive elements, not whole windows.
fixes.correct: Floating glass windows in your room; controls light up when you look at them.

note: Sourcing solid; plain line slightly misdescribes the hover effect.

sources.note: E Ink: microcapsules holding white and black charged particles; Spectra built for electronic shelf labels.
Waveshare: bistable, reflective, no backlight; full refresh about 2-4 s with flashing; ghosting after partial refresh; unsuitable for animation; 4-grey mode on one panel; Spectra 6 dithering.

fixes.problem: 'Very few grey levels' generalises from one hobby panel's 4-grey mode; e-reader and Kaleido panels show 16 grey levels.
fixes.correct: Limited greys: 16 levels on e-reader panels, as few as 2-4 on small hobby panels; colour panels show a handful of inks with dithering.

note: Two working sources; grey-level claim understated.

sources.note: Wikipedia TUI: blue background with white or yellow characters, CP437 box drawing, Norton Commander, WordPerfect, Turbo Vision IDEs.
Wikipedia Turbo Vision: Borland, circa 1990, list boxes, check boxes, radio buttons, menus with mouse support.
int10h blocks curl (403) but loads via WebFetch: DOS-era text-mode fonts including IBM VGA 8x16, CC BY-SA 4.0.

fixes.problem: WebTUI is a modern terminal-UI CSS library (Gruvbox/Nord-style themes, vim-like layouts), not the DOS blue-screen text-mode look.
fixes.correct: Drop it or label it as a general terminal-UI kit; the Turbo Vision port is the faithful example.

note: Facts verified; one example belongs to a different terminal look.

sources.note: Wikipedia Monochrome monitor: common 1960s-1980s; P1 green, P3 amber, P4 page white; amber seen as easier on the eyes.
CSS-Tricks: radial green glow, text-shadow 0 0 5px, repeating 1px/2px line gradient.
cool-retro-term README: mimics old cathode tube screens; Default Amber and Default Green profiles.

note: All claims and the example verified.

sources.note: Fast Company 2015 (archived): terminal on market since December 1982; dense tabular text with charts; amber on black by default; keyboard keys EQUITY, GOVT, NEWS; users notice small font changes.
UX Magazine, March 2010: black background with yellow and orange text; users take pride in the complex interface.
Core77, May 2013: two-, four- or six-monitor setups.

note: All claims verified; amber hex in code is marked inferred, not Bloomberg's.

sources.note: Vitsoe: ten principles from the late 1970s; neutral and restrained; as little design as possible; Braun products from 1958 onward.
V&A: ET66, 1987, Rams and Lubs; black number keys, brown operator keys, yellow equals.
MAK Frankfurt: ET 66, Kronberg, 1987; colour-coded buttons; convex buttons. It does not mention a strict grid.

fixes.problem: 'on a strict grid' is not in S3 or the other sources.
fixes.correct: Round, slightly convex buttons [S3]; mark the grid [inferred] or cite a source.

note: Museum-grade sources; one small unsupported detail.

sources.note: Metropolis: brushed aluminium case, small colour display, four coloured knobs with matching colour-coded display, graphics recalling early Nintendo 8-bit characters.
Wikipedia OP-1: prototype at NAMM 2010, released 2011, 320 x 160 OLED with mode graphics, 'limitations' quote.

fixes.problem: 'geometric motifs' is not in S1, which describes characters (gorillas, a Karl Marx likeness) per mode.
fixes.correct: Screen graphics are playful characters, one set per mode, recalling early 8-bit game art.

note: Rests on one product; two working sources support it.

sources.note: HUDS+GUIS book page: FUI mixes film, storytelling, motion graphics, UX and UI.
Mark Coleran: set lighting washes out screens, primary display colours look stronger; green dated, red militaristic, leaving blue.
Noessel: one film's SHIELD screens are strictly orange or strictly blue, meant to be seen not read; fuidget-filled. It is one production, not a general rule.
Arwes README: futuristic sci-fi designs, animations and sound effects; now states it is no longer maintained.

fixes.problem: 'Often one hue per screen' generalises from a single film's screens.
fixes.correct: Some productions keep each screen to one hue (all orange or all blue), made to be glanced at rather than read.

fixes.problem: Arwes is real but its README says the project is no longer maintained.
fixes.correct: Keep it, noting it is unmaintained.

note: Well sourced; soften one generalisation and flag Arwes as unmaintained.

sources.note: Palm OS Programmer's Companion: 160x160 LCD, 1 bit/pixel until OS 3.0, rounded-rectangle buttons that invert, popup dialogs at the bottom using full width. URL now redirects to users.fuw.edu.pl; update it.
Zen of Palm PDF: 80/20 rule, focus on what users do 80 percent of the time; common functions one tap away.

note: Verified; only the S1 host moved (redirect works).

sources.note: Iwata Asks: rows of TVs in an electronics shop led to panes and the word Channel; three rows of four channels treated equally.
Wikipedia Wii Menu: first release 19 November 2006, four pages of 4x3 grids, 48 slots, time and date, Wii Remote pointer.

note: Both sources load and support every sourced claim.
